title: Two Heads in a Row
statement: You flip a fair coin until you get two heads in a row. What is the expected number of flips?
insight: Only your progress toward HH matters, so define the expected remaining flips from each progress state and condition on the next flip.
redHerring: Guessing 4 because P(HH) = 1/4 on any given pair of flips. Overlapping pairs are not independent trials.
hints: What is the only thing about the history that matters for the future?
Let $E_0$ be the expected flips from scratch and $E_1$ the expected flips when the last flip was H.
Condition on the next flip: $E_1 = 1 + \tfrac12\cdot 0 + \tfrac12 E_0$.
solution:
Let $E_0$ = expected flips from a fresh start, $E_1$ = expected flips when the previous flip was H.

$E_0 = 1 + \tfrac12 E_1 + \tfrac12 E_0$ and $E_1 = 1 + \tfrac12\cdot 0 + \tfrac12 E_0$.

Substituting: $E_0 = 1 + \tfrac12(1+\tfrac12E_0) + \tfrac12E_0$, so $\tfrac14 E_0 = \tfrac32$ and $E_0 = 6$.
